newsitem.title: JAPAN: IWCC sees refined copper output growth in '97,'98.
newsitem.headline: IWCC sees refined copper output growth in '97,'98.

text.p: Global refined copper production will rise to 13,145,000 tonnes in 1997 and to 13,896,000 tonnes in 1998, compared with 12,349,000 tonnes last year, according to International Wrought Copper Council (IWCC) statistics.
The steady growth is mainly due to increased output in Chile, the United States and India, the IWCC data, obtained by Reuters on Tuesday, showed.

Chilean production will increase to 2,136,000 tonnes this year and to 2,428,000 tonnes in 1998, compared with 1,756,000 tonnes last year, the data showed. Output from the United States will reach 2,420,000 tonnes this year and 2,510,000 tonnes next year, up from 2,340,000 tonnes in 1996, it showed.
Refined copper output in India will grow to 75,000 tonnes this year and surge to 140,000 tonnes next year, compared with 39,000 tonnes in 1996, the statistics showed.

The IWCC's copper statistics were compiled during its 53rd joint meeting with copper producing and marketing companies in Kobe, western Japan, last week. A copy of the data was obtained by Reuters through local metal industry sources.
